terms.gloss: one’s favourite, darling, delight (a person, a place, a thing)
evidence: Plin. Ep. 1.3.1: Cōmum, tuae meaeque dēliciae
terms.comment: To be someone’s favourite is in dēliciīs esse alicui (Lewis & Short). Titus was amor ac dēliciae generis hūmānī (Suet. Tit. 1, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: is my favourite, I like it best
terms.comment: Latin has no adjective for “favourite”; it says what pleases most, as in the household question Quid tibi maximē placuit? (see what did you like best?).

phrases.latin: quid agit Cōmum, tuae meaeque dēliciae?
phrases.english: how is Comum, your favourite place and mine?

sources: Lewis & Short: deliciae · Lewis & Short: placeo · Lewis & Short: carus
